title: What do we know about whole numbers multiplied when they are in a row?
description: Two, three, four and five whole numbers in a row are multiplied, and each answer is shown to be a multiple of two, six, twenty four and one hundred and twenty. The reason is which multiples must appear among the numbers in a row. The method is the same as the examples in the book on multiples and factors.
teaching_notes: One idea: among numbers in a row an even number comes every second place, a multiple of three every third and a multiple of four every fourth, so certain factors must be there. Watch for students who check one set of numbers and decide the answer is always a multiple.

video_script.why: A learner sees which multiples must appear among two, three, four and five whole numbers in a row, and so which numbers always divide their answer when multiplied.
video_script.substitution: the book's own question on two, three, four and five whole numbers in a row multiplied together
video_script.anchor: a number line with the even numbers, multiples of three and multiples of four marked, as in the book's rows
video_script.payoff_line: Two numbers in a row always give a multiple of two. Three give a multiple of six.

final_answer.value: Always a multiple of 2, of 6, of 24 and of 120 respectively
final_answer.spoken: two numbers in a row always give a multiple of two, three give a multiple of six, four give a multiple of twenty four, and five give a multiple of one hundred and twenty

hold_back: Always a multiple of 2, of 6, of 24 and of 120 respectively
maths_rules: two in a row: one is even, so the answer is a multiple of 2; 3 x 4 = 12
three in a row: one is a multiple of 3 and at least one is even; 2 and 3 share no factor, so a multiple of 6; 4 x 5 x 6 = 120
four in a row: two are even, one of them a multiple of 4, so a multiple of 4 x 2 = 8 from the evens; one is a multiple of 3; 8 and 3 share no factor, so a multiple of 24; 1 x 2 x 3 x 4 = 24
five in a row: also a multiple of 5; 24 and 5 share no factor, so a multiple of 120; 1 x 2 x 3 x 4 x 5 = 120
video_script.design: One idea: among numbers in a row certain multiples must appear. Assumes factors and multiples. The number line with the marks stays on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about whole numbers in a row.
<bookmark mark='groups'/>We will solve it the same way as the examples in your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>When two numbers in a row are multiplied, is the answer always a multiple of two? What about three, four and five numbers in a row?

beats.on_screen: the number line and brackets stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: on the number line, evens marked every 2nd place, multiples of 3 every 3rd place, multiples of 4 every 4th place

marks.evens: the even numbers are marked on the number line, one in every second place
marks.more: multiples of three and of four are marked in their own colours

narration: <bookmark mark='evens'/>On a number line, an even number comes in every second place.
<bookmark mark='more'/>A multiple of three comes every third place, and a multiple of four every fourth place.

beats.on_screen: Given: two, three, four and five whole numbers in a row, multiplied together

marks.given: the four cases are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, there are two, three, four and five whole numbers in a row, multiplied together.

beats.on_screen: To find: which numbers always divide each answer, and why
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which numbers always divide each answer, and why.

beats.on_screen: two in a row: one is even, so the answer is a multiple of 2. 3 × 4 = 12

marks.even: two numbers in a row are bracketed and the even one is lit

narration: <bookmark mark='even'/>Step one, take two numbers in a row. One of them is even, so the answer has the factor two.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Three times four is twelve, a multiple of two.

beats.on_screen: three in a row: one is a multiple of 3, at least one is even; 2 and 3 share no factor; multiple of 6. 4 × 5 × 6 = 120

marks.three: three numbers in a row are bracketed, with the multiple of three lit
marks.six: the even number and the multiple of three give the factors two and three, so six
marks.ex: four times five times six shows one hundred and twenty

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step two, take three numbers in a row. One is a multiple of three, and at least one is even.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Two and three share no factor, so the answer is a multiple of six.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Four times five times six is one hundred and twenty, a multiple of six.

beats.on_screen: four in a row: two evens, one a multiple of 4: factor 8; a multiple of 3; 8 and 3 share no factor; multiple of 24. 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 = 24

marks.evens: four numbers in a row are bracketed, with two even numbers lit and one of them a multiple of four
marks.eight: the two even numbers give a multiple of eight and the multiple of three is lit
marks.twentyfour: eight and three give a multiple of twenty four
marks.ex: one times two times three times four shows twenty four

narration: <bookmark mark='evens'/>Step three, take four numbers in a row. Two are even, and one of those is a multiple of four.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>The two even numbers give a multiple of eight, and one number is a multiple of three.
<bookmark mark='twentyfour'/>Eight and three share no factor, so the answer is a multiple of twenty four.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>One times two times three times four is twenty four.

beats.on_screen: five in a row: also a multiple of 5; 24 and 5 share no factor; multiple of 120. 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 × 5 = 120

marks.five: five numbers in a row are bracketed, with the multiple of five lit
marks.share: twenty four and five are shown sharing no factor, giving one hundred and twenty
marks.ex: one times two times three times four times five shows one hundred and twenty

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step four, take five numbers in a row. They hold a multiple of five as well.
<bookmark mark='share'/>Twenty four and five share no factor, so the answer is a multiple of one hundred and twenty.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>One times two times three times four times five is one hundred and twenty.

marks.go: six times seven times eight times nine times ten shows thirty thousand two hundred and forty
marks.div: it is shown as one hundred and twenty times two hundred and fifty two

narration: <bookmark mark='go'/>Step five, put other numbers back to check. Take six, seven, eight, nine and ten, multiplied together.
<bookmark mark='div'/>The answer is thirty thousand two hundred and forty. That is one hundred and twenty times two hundred and fifty two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Always a multiple of 2, of 6, of 24 and of 120 respectively

marks.rest: the four results are lit in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Two numbers in a row always give a multiple of two. Three give a multiple of six.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Four give a multiple of twenty four. Five give a multiple of one hundred and twenty.
